name: Tomato Rice
cuisine: South Indian (Tamil thakkali sadam; close cousin of Karnataka tomato bath, a lunchbox and "variety rice" staple)

ingredients.name: Raw rice (sona masoori; basmati also works)

equipment: Bowl and strainer for washing and soaking the rice
Ladle or flat spatula (a fork for fluffing)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teacup and teaspoons are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Wash the rice
steps.text: Put 75 g (about ⅓ cup + 1 tbsp) rice in a bowl, cover with water, swirl and drain. Repeat 2 more times.
steps.visualCue: The last rinse water is only slightly cloudy.
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with the last rinse water
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling rice in cloudy water.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover with fresh water and leave for 10 min, then drain fully.
steps.tip: For basmati, soak 20 min. Soaking keeps the grains whole and separate.
steps.visualCue: The grains look whiter and slightly plumper.
steps.cameraCheck: The drained rice in the strainer
steps.videoShot: Water draining from the rice through a strainer.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Thinly slice 50 g onion (½ medium).
steps.visualCue: Thin half-moon slices.
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced onion on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife slicing onion into thin strips.

steps.title: Chop the tomatoes
steps.text: Finely chop 130 g tomatoes (2 small).
steps.tip: Ripe, deep-red tomatoes give the best colour. For a smoother, kid-friendly rice, purée them instead.
steps.visualCue: Small, juicy pieces with their juice on the board.
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped tomatoes
steps.videoShot: Knife dicing a red tomato.

steps.title: Prep the greens
steps.text: Slit 1 green chilli lengthwise, pick 8–10 curry leaves and chop 1 tbsp coriander leaves.
steps.visualCue: Three small heaps ready on the board.
steps.cameraCheck: The chilli, curry leaves and coriander
steps.videoShot: A green chilli being slit open.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the open cooker on medium heat and add 2 tsp (10 g) groundnut oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily.
steps.cameraCheck: The hot oil in the cooker
steps.videoShot: Oil sliding across the cooker base.

steps.title: Add mustard seeds
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp mustard seeds.
steps.visualCue: The seeds crackle and pop.
steps.cameraCheck: The popping seeds
steps.videoShot: Mustard seeds spluttering in oil.

steps.title: Add the dals
steps.text: Add 1 tsp chana dal and ½ tsp urad dal; stir.
steps.tip: Lower the heat if they brown too fast; burnt dals taste bitter.
steps.visualCue: The dals turn light golden and smell nutty.
steps.cameraCheck: The golden dals in the oil
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring yellow and white dals turning golden.

steps.title: Add whole spices
steps.text: Add the 1 cm cinnamon, 2 cloves and 1 bay leaf.
steps.visualCue: A warm, sweet spice smell.
steps.cameraCheck: The whole spices in the oil
steps.videoShot: Cinnamon and cloves dropping into the oil.

steps.title: Add curry leaves and chilli
steps.text: Add the curry leaves and slit green chilli.
steps.tip: Stand back; wet curry leaves spit.
steps.visualCue: The leaves crackle and turn bright green.
steps.cameraCheck: The tempering in the cooker
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves sizzling.

steps.title: Sauté the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring often.
steps.visualCue: Soft, translucent, just turning light golden at the edges.
steps.cameraCheck: The onion in the cooker
steps.videoShot: A spatula turning golden onion slices.

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell has gone.
steps.cameraCheck: The onion with the paste mixed in
steps.videoShot: Paste melting into the onions.

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps.text: Add the chopped tomatoes and 2 g (a level ⅓ tsp) salt. Cover for 2 min, then uncover and mash with the spatula, cooking until fully broken down.
steps.tip: This is the key step. Undercooked tomatoes make the rice taste raw and sour.
steps.visualCue: A thick, mushy, jammy masala; tiny drops of oil appear at the edges.
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato masala in the cooker
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing tomatoes into a pulp.

steps.title: Add the ground spices
steps.text: Add a large pinch turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder and a pinch of garam masala. Stir on low heat.
steps.visualCue: The masala turns deep red-orange and smells toasty.
steps.cameraCheck: The spiced masala
steps.videoShot: Red and yellow powders stirred into the tomato masala.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Add the drained rice and stir gently to coat it in the masala.
steps.tip: Stir gently so the soaked grains don't break.
steps.visualCue: Every grain is coated orange; no wet white grains.
steps.cameraCheck: The coated rice in the cooker
steps.videoShot: A spatula folding rice into the red masala.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Pour in 150 ml (about ⅔ cup) water, stir, scrape the bottom and taste the water for salt.
steps.tip: Basmati needs about 130 ml. For a softer, Tamil-mess style, use 180 ml.
steps.visualCue: The water stands about 1 cm above the rice; the bottom is clean; the water tastes slightly salty.
steps.cameraCheck: The open cooker with rice and water
steps.videoShot: Water pouring in and a spatula scraping the base.

steps.title: Add half the coriander and close
steps.text: Sprinkle in half the chopped coriander, close the lid and cook on medium heat for 2 whistles, then switch off.
steps.visualCue: You have counted 2 whistles.
steps.cameraCheck: The closed cooker on the stove
steps.videoShot: Steam puffing out with a whistle.

steps.title: Let the pressure drop
steps.text: Leave the cooker closed until the pressure falls on its own.
steps.tip: Opening early makes the rice wet and mushy.
steps.visualCue: The weight lifts easily with no hiss.
steps.cameraCheck: The cooker with the lid off
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting off to show orange-red rice.

steps.title: Fluff
steps.text: Fluff gently with a fork and sprinkle the rest of the coriander; remove the bay leaf and cinnamon if you like.
steps.visualCue: Separate, soft, evenly orange grains with green flecks.
steps.cameraCheck: A forkful of rice lifted from the cooker
steps.videoShot: A fork lifting fluffy tomato rice.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: A mound of moist, glossy, red-orange rice.
steps.cameraCheck: The served plate
steps.videoShot: Tomato rice on a steel plate with raita and papad beside it.

reasons: boiled in a pressure cooker, with modest unsaturated oil, no dairy, no added sugar and about 180 g of tomato and onion, which bring potassium, vitamin C, lycopene and about 6 g fibre (est.). Against it: it is mostly white-rice starch (about 72 g carbs) with a high glycaemic response and only about 9 g protein, and 2 g salt gives about 40% of the day's sodium. Restaurant and mess versions often use more oil or ghee and cashews, more salt, and come with fried fryums or papad.

researchRating.basis: a well-loved, everyday South Indian "variety rice" with recipes on every major Indian recipe site (Swasthi's, Hebbar's Kitchen, Veg Recipes of India, Tarla Dalal, Jeyashri's Kitchen, Raks Kitchen, Archana's Kitchen) and coverage in international food media (MasterClass, Milk Street, Saveur), praised as a quick, cheap lunchbox meal. Deduction because it is seen as a simple home or mess dish rather than a treat, it is rarely ordered in Mumbai (few menu listings), and the star counts on the main recipe pages could not be seen from this environment.

storage: Cool and refrigerate within 1 hour (cooked rice can grow Bacillus cereus if left warm). Fridge: up to 1–2 days in an airtight box. Freezer: up to 1 month in a flat freezer bag. To reheat, sprinkle 1–2 tbsp water, cover and microwave for 1½–2 min, stirring halfway, until steaming hot throughout; or warm in a covered pan on low heat for 3–4 min. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: Tomato rice tikkis. Mash 1 cup cold leftover tomato rice with 2 tbsp besan (gram flour), 1 tbsp chopped coriander and a pinch of chilli flakes; shape into 4 small patties and shallow-fry on a tawa with 1 tsp oil, 2–3 min a side, until crisp and golden. Serve with green chutney or ketchup: soft rice turned into a crunchy snack, and it stays gluten-free and vegan.
burnOff: about 6.2 km of running (435 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.7 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 45 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With raita and a roasted papad (about +100 kcal), add about 1.5 km of running.

navratri.reason: rice, onion, garlic and table salt are avoided on the common North and West Indian vrat rule set; a samak-rice (barnyard millet) tomato pulao with sendha namak is the usual swap, but that is a different dish

ekadashi.reason: rice and dals (chana and urad dal in the tempering) are the main foods given up on Ekadashi

jain.reason: skip onion, garlic and ginger; tomato, rice, dried spices and curry leaves fit common Jain practice (see the Jain variant)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so there is no halal concern; filling and easy to digest, but low in protein (about 9 g) and moderately salty (about 2 g salt), so for sehri pair it with curd, dal or eggs and drink water

jain.reason: skip the onion and ginger-garlic paste; tomato, rice, dals, green chilli, dried spices and curry leaves stay (onion, garlic and ginger are roots/bulbs avoided in Jain food)

vegan.reason: groundnut oil, no ghee, curd, honey or other animal products

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg, so it fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: skip the onion and ginger-garlic paste; add 1 tsp grated ginger only if your family allows it

glutenFree.reason: rice, dals, vegetables and spices only; no hing is used (most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so if you add hing, use one labelled gluten-free)

dairyFree.reason: cooked in oil, no ghee, butter or curd (serve with a dairy-free side if you need it fully dairy-free)

description: A vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free one-pot South Indian rice cooked in a spiced tomato-onion masala; Jain and sattvik versions below.

variants.name: Jain Tomato Rice (no onion, garlic or ginger)

variants.reason: . Main recipe already vegan (groundnut oil, no ghee or dairy). If you add the optional ghee on top, skip it.
. Main recipe already gluten-free (no hing, wheat or rava). If you add hing, use one labelled gluten-free.
. Main recipe already dairy-free; serve without curd or raita, or with a dairy-free side.
